top.para: A pen on 19 printed pages became a record of 143 notes, each page drawn three ways, 11 readings asked not guessed, four decisions with their provenance, and a review hub: a handwritten review as traceable as a pull request.

in-short.para: 19 pages and 143 notes; a record; questions not guesses; decisions; the voice; the hub; traceability.

setup.line: A café, a pen and 168 pages
setup.para: The printed release candidate, 19 pages read with a pen, photographed in four batches; this goes past the habit described in Reading with a pen again.

reading.para: Every note word for word with place and meaning, each page drawn three ways, eleven uncertain readings sent back as questions and answered by voice.

asked.para: The voice (32 notes), the reader's context (21), the making-of out of the way, topics first, show the book, fact or opinion, QR codes, and ticks for what works.

decisions.line: When a margin note is a decision
decisions.para: 016 a release is a release, 017 a new book, 018 two editions, 019 the title: each recorded with the page and note that made it.

room.para: A margin system marking fact and opinion, and seven working QR codes resolving to the book's site.

hub.para: Asked whether all pages were tracked, the agent built a hub with every note addressable, and a build rule that keeps notes from being lost.

shows.para: A handwritten review made as traceable as a pull request, with the pen still the best way to think while reading.

status.para: Stopped at page 19 of 168; changes planned, no third candidate yet; the method now used on the book of the talk.

limits.para: 19 pages reviewed; counts from the book site's record; one hand read; my interest.

sources.para: The book site's four-part record, decisions page, hub and co-written article, and my messages of 31 October.
